questions.q: What is the defining characteristic of a Primary Key in a relational database table?
options: It can repeat across multiple rows
It must contain a unique value for each row and cannot be null
It must always be a text string
It links to a table in a different database
A key used to encrypt the entire database
A column in one table that points back to the Primary Key of another table, creating a link between them
The very first column created in any table
A key that only works for foreign (non-US) clients

questions.q: What is the purpose of Data Normalization?
options: To make queries run slower on purpose
To organize a database to reduce redundancy -- avoiding storing the same data in multiple places -- so updates only need to happen in one location
To convert all data into JSON format
To delete unused tables automatically

questions.q: Which SQL command corresponds to the 'Read' action in CRUD?
options: INSERT INTO
SELECT
UPDATE
DELETE

questions.q: What does the SQL WHERE clause do?
options: Deletes the entire table
Filters the results to only include rows that meet a specific condition
Sorts the results alphabetically
Creates a new table

questions.q: What does the SQL JOIN command do?
options: Deletes duplicate rows automatically
Combines columns from two or more tables based on a related column (like linking HighScores to Users)
Merges two entire databases into one file
Joins a user's browser session to the server

ch14_lab_security.title: Quick Check: SQL Injection, Hashing & Privacy Law

questions.q: How do professional developers prevent SQL Injection attacks?
options: By making the database password longer
By using Parameterized Queries to sanitize inputs, treating them as harmless text rather than executable commands
By hiding the database on a different server
By disabling all SELECT queries

questions.q: What does adding a 'Salt' to a password hash accomplish?
options: It makes the password taste better to hackers (a joke term with no real function)
It adds random characters to the password before hashing, so two users with the same password end up with completely different hashes
It deletes the password after one use
It converts the password into a Primary Key

questions.q: Under GDPR's 'Data Minimization' principle, what should a developer do when designing a database?
options: Collect as much user data as possible in case it's needed later
Only collect the data you actually need -- e.g., don't store a full birth date if all you need is whether the user is 18+
Store every field as plain text for easy access
Only apply this rule to companies based in the EU
